- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`, `packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin b38533b0c17392f1f004a3f2c2407973591e669e && git checkout b38533b0c17392f1f004a3f2c2407973591e669e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65 5f35aff38a34a4aa5b170d2803e12ce43b3d0dcd && git checkout -B drift-repro 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65 && git merge --no-ff 5f35aff38a34a4aa5b170d2803e12ce43b3d0dcd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f35aff38a34a4aa5b170d2803e12ce43b3d0dcd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-membership-keys.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts (read, unchanged: `compileFilter` and the bag merge), packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts (read, unchanged), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts (read, unchanged), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (read, unchanged: the manifest `extend` path), packages/spec/liveness/object.json, .changeset/25234-membership-keys-staged.md, the two new test suites

Judged against ruling 6355640929 (letter A, riders 1 to 4), design 6344270438 and landing plan 6370632236 on card #25234. Inputs: the card body and all 10 comments, the PR body, its 17-file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge base `74496c64`, and the 42 check-runs on the head (36 success, 6 skipped, all six opt-in or matrix shells; 0 failed). The remainder of the diff (4 generated reference pages, `state-counts/object.md`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

**Spec hits (the `hits` paths).** `object.zod.ts` changes the `membershipKeys` TSDoc and `describe` text only; `rls.zod.ts` changes two docblocks only. No key, type, refinement, default or export moves: the accept set is unchanged, the describe now states the contract the reader meets instead of "not applied yet", and the 4 regenerated reference pages carry the same sentence. **Right.** `MEMBERSHIP_KEY_MAX_VALUES = 1000` (rls.zod.ts:798) stays the one constant, not authorable, as the ruling's sub-fork 2 fixed it.

**Liveness.** `membershipKeys` and its 5 children flip `planned` to `live`, `authorWarn` / `authorHint` dropped in the same edit as PR 1's note asked. Every evidence anchor named exists on this head (`stageRlsMembership` in security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, `stageDeclaredMembershipKeys`, `readDeclaredKey`, `describeMembershipKeyDeclaration` in object-membership-keys.ts, `membershipKeySource` in explain-engine.ts). `Spec property liveness` check green. **Right.**

**The reader (plugin-security), judged against the ruling and its riders:**

- *Every miss fails closed.* `readDeclaredKey` returns `unresolved` for no user, tenant wall `deny`, filter refused, over the bound (rows or flattened values), and a thrown read or schema load; `stageOneKey` returns `unresolved` for a key two registry objects declare and for a resolver collision. Only a `resolved` outcome writes the bag; a zero-row read writes `[]`. Downstream, `compileFilter` (rls-compiler.ts:1071 to 1086) turns an unresolved variable or an empty set into `deniedBy` and, with no granting sibling, `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, with the existing WARN. The `filter` is judged by the same `compileFilter` with an empty principal context and X's field guard, so `current_user.*` inside it, a phantom column and a non-lowering shape all land on `RLS_DENY_FILTER` and are treated as a miss; `null` is also treated as a miss, which is the safe reading of a return that otherwise means "nothing applied". **Right.** Pinned by the real-engine suite (1,001 rows red / 1,000 green; `current_user` filter; phantom column; declared twice; collision; CONTROL no-declaration reads zero rows).
- *The roster read is confined to the caller's own tenant wall, with no platform-admin crossing (rider 1).* The wall is `computeTenantLayer0Verdict(tenantLayer0InputOf({..., isPlatformAdmin: false}))`. In `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` (core) the only crossing is `isPlatformAdmin && posturePermitsCrossTenant`; with `isPlatformAdmin` pinned false the `none` outcomes left are structural (single posture, tenancy disabled, object without `organization_id`), exactly the cases where the read door applies no wall to X either; `isolated` with no active org and `group` with an empty access set give `deny`, which is a miss. The find runs under `context: { isSystem: true }` with no `tenantId`, so the `where` carries the wall as its only org scope and the middleware's total `isSystem` bypass keeps X's own row policies (which may read this very key) out of the read: no cycle, no caller posture, no audience. **Right.** Pinned: the unit test asserts byte-identical `find` arguments (`where` with the org term, `fields`, `limit`, `context`) for MEMBER, EXTERNAL/external, PLATFORM_ADMIN with `admin_full_access`, and TENANT_ADMIN; the real-engine test shows the portal set's own roster read is `PERMISSION_DENIED` while its PO read resolves the key, and a roster row in organisation Y never counts.
- *Audience-neutral (rider 2).* No code path reads `audience` or `posture`; MEMBER, external and TENANT_ADMIN resolve the same rows (pinned). **Right.**
- *The bound is enforced.* `limit: MEMBERSHIP_KEY_MAX_VALUES + 1`; more than 1,000 rows, or more than 1,000 distinct values after flattening a multi-valued F, is `over-bound`. **Right.**
- *A collision is refused, not shadowed.* `resolverOwns` is `resolver.keys` includes the key OR the resolver staged it on this request (`noteResolverStagedKeys`); on a hit the resolver's bag value is deleted before Layer 1 compiles, the outcome is `unresolved`, and an error names both owners once per logger and again at boot (`SecurityPlugin.start` via `resolverCollisionsOf`). A key two objects declare resolves from none of them. The one case left as-is is a bag value the resolver did not supply: `rlsMembership` is a `NonEntryExecutionContextField` in core's `assemble-execution-context.ts`, so no transport entry point assembles it from a request; it is server-constructed, and leaving it is the resolver's existing precedence. **Right**, and declared in the PR body.
- *Lazy, per key, per request.* Keys are read off the policies' `using` and `check` through `parseCelToAst(sqlPredicateToCel(...))`, reserved kernel names excluded; the memo is a WeakMap on the execution context; both compile sites (`computeLayeredRlsFilter` before Layer 1, `computeWriteCheckFilter` with `withCheck`) call `stageRlsMembership(context, policies, object)`. **Right**; one read across `qa_po` + `qa_asn` pinned, zero reads for a key-free policy pinned.
- *Nothing an ordinary object without `membershipKeys` does changes.* `stageDeclaredMembershipKeys` returns before touching state when no policy reads a non-reserved `current_user.*` name; a read of an undeclared key returns `undefined` with no log and no bag write, so the compiler's existing WARN/deny path is untouched; `stageResolverMembership` is the old body plus bookkeeping; `tenantLayer0InputOf` reproduces the read door's former input literal term for term (`posturePermitsCrossTenant` = `isPrivate || tenancyDisabled || isBetterAuthManaged`, as at origin/main:168); explain adds text and `via` only when `membershipKeyOutcomesFor` returns outcomes (CONTROL pinned at object and record level). **Right.** The declared-key staging also does not alter the compiler's reserved-name refusal at rls-compiler.ts:985 to 991.
- *Explain (rider 3).* Object-level `detail` names the key with label/description, X, F, U, the filter, the resolved size or the miss reason, then "Whoever can write X can grant this key" with the permission sets `checkObjectPermission` grants `insert` or `update` on X. Record-level `business_rls` rule carries `via: 'membership:KEY'` and names the linking roster row from the staging read's `id` projection (no second read). `ExplainDecision` gains no field. **Right.** Observation, not a defect: when a record is excluded or no value links, `via` still names the first key the object's policies read; the design asked for `via` on the policy's rule and this is that.

**objectql `extend` door (landing-plan item 2).** `registerObject` refuses an `ownership: 'extend'` contribution carrying `membershipKeys` beside the `defaultRowScope` refusal, `INVALID_METADATA` / 422, name `ExtensionMembershipKeysRefusedError`. Measured on this head: `mergeObjectDefinitions` (registry.ts:432 to 466) copies only `fields`, `validations`, `indexes`, `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, so the key was being dropped in silence (ADR-0078); the manifest path (plugin.ts:9322 to 9335) copies a closed key list and `ObjectExtensionSchema` is strict, so the direct `registerObject` call was the only door. `EXTENSION_MEMBERSHIP_KEYS_REFUSED_CODE` is not re-exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` (nor is its `defaultRowScope` sibling), so no public surface moves. **Right.** 6 tests, 2 controls.

**Public surface.** `object-membership-keys.ts` is not re-exported from plugin-security's index; `SecurityPlugin.stageRlsMembership` is private and its new parameters are optional. No published accept set or public surface widens or narrows. **`Clause-②: no` is right.**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25234-membership-keys-staged.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` **minor**, `@objectstack/objectql` **patch**, `@objectstack/spec` **patch**. Both declaration lines are present in the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`.

- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the right kind: no key is added, refused or tombstoned; the meaning of an authorable key (`membershipKeys`) moves from "declared, not applied" to "applied", which is the `semantic` definition in AGENTS.md.
- Under the ruled level rule (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: a kind other than `none` asks for at least one moved package at `minor`+; `semantic` under a bare `no` is a kind like the others), plugin-security `minor` satisfies it; objectql and spec, which publish no surface change, take `patch`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no` with no arm matches ①: the accept set and public surface are unchanged.

Clause-②: no — right as declared; the diff publishes no accept-set or public-surface change.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **PR body: "This head already merged `main` at `aa2dbab7`."** Stale. The head's second parent is `74496c64` (`git show 5f35aff3 --format=%P`), which is also the merge base against `origin/main`; `aa2dbab7` was the earlier merge (`21cace53`). The dev records the correction in os-dev-report 6374979058 (the relay has no PR-edit op). Every other body statement I could check holds: 17 files, +1493 / −79 (sums of the file list), check-runs 36/6/0, the fail-closed table, the pins, the deviations. The body's suite counts (219 files / 4594) are the pre-merge run and the report's (220 / 4607) the post-merge run; both are labelled as such, so not a second stale statement. **Answered, not blocking**; the seat may ask the dev to edit the line when the relay allows.
2. **Rider 4 (serial with #25233).** PR #25515 (`9019af9f`) is an ancestor of the merged `74496c64` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` yes); this PR landed second and merged `main` after it, as the rider orders. **Answered.**
3. **Deviation: `tenantLayer0InputOf` extracted.** Read term for term against origin/main's inlined literal: identical inputs, so the read door's wall is unchanged. **Answered.**
4. **Deviation: no `tenantId` on the system context.** The `where` carries the caller's Layer 0 as the only org scope (unit pin asserts the org term); with a `tenantId` the engine would have narrowed a `group` key to the active org below the wall. **Answered**; the direction is correct and the pin holds it.
5. **Tier H `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` row.** Not in this diff (no `skills/**` path; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). The re-worded `live` text is in the PR body and report 6374979058 for the seat to land as its own governed PR, per landing plan 6370632236. **Carried forward, not this PR's.**
6. **PR 3 dependencies.** The publish-time refusals 5 to 7 and 11 to 13 (field types, `filter` lowering, policy comparison) are the authoring rules' (PR 3), as the ruling orders; until then a wrong declaration fails closed at runtime with a WARN, which is this PR's contract. **Open by design, not a flag on this PR.**
7. **`open_questions`: none** in report 6374979058. The design's dependency on #25233 (premise 5) is settled by the ruling itself (EXTERNAL rung evaluates RLS).
8. **Observation (no action).** `readDeclaredKey` keeps only string values of F; a non-string value is dropped, which narrows (fails closed), never widens.
